transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I keep hearing things that no one else seems to hear, and it’s starting to really bother me at work and at home.
Besides hearing these voices, have you also been experiencing periods where your mood is extremely elevated, or alternatively, very low and hopeless for a significant amount of time?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme mood swings, like feeling super high or deeply hopeless. It's more that I just feel flat and indifferent, and I've really lacked the motivation to do much of anything lately.
Besides the voices and feeling indifferent, have you noticed any decline in your ability to take care of yourself, organize your thoughts, or communicate clearly with others?

Yes, communicating has become really hard because it feels like too much effort to get the words out, so I mostly give short answers or stay quiet. I've also had moments where I freeze up or feel this strong urge to tap and line up items at the register, which makes organizing my actions feel slow and disrupted.
Have these voices and the difficulty with your thoughts been present consistently for at least six months, and do the voices ever comment on your actions or argue with each other?

The voice and the freezing at the register have actually only been a steady problem for about three months, though my lack of motivation and social withdrawal have been building for over two years. The voice does comment on what I'm doing—like saying "You messed that up"—but it's just a single low male voice, so there aren't multiple voices arguing with each other.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being broadcast out loud for others to hear, or that someone is putting thoughts directly into your mind that aren't your own?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never felt like my thoughts were being broadcasted for others to hear, nor have I felt like anyone was putting thoughts into my head.
Do you have any strong, unshakable beliefs that someone is plotting against you, spying on you, or that there is a specific hidden meaning behind everyday events?

No, I don't feel like anyone is plotting against me or spying on me. My main concerns are really just the voice I hear and those moments where I freeze up. I don't think there is any hidden meaning behind everyday events.
Did these experiences with the voice and the freezing start suddenly over the course of a few days, or did they develop more gradually over several weeks?

They definitely developed more gradually over time rather than starting suddenly. While the voice and the freezing at the register became a steady, daily problem over the last three months, the broader changes in my motivation and behavior have actually been slowly building up for over two years.
Besides the auditory hallucinations and the freezing episodes, have you noticed any other unusual movements or physical postures that you seem unable to control or that feel repetitive?

Yes, I get this uncontrollable urge to tap items three times before I can bag them at the register. Other times, I feel like I have to line them up in a very precise pattern first. It happens even when there's a line forming, and I know it looks really strange to others.

When you perform these tapping and lining-up rituals, do you feel like you are doing them to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce anxiety, or does it feel more like an automatic, mechanical movement that you simply cannot stop?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it in those terms. It doesn't feel like I'm trying to prevent something bad from happening, but more like an overwhelming, strange urge to tap and line things up that is just very hard to resist.

When you are performing these tapping and lining-up rituals, do you feel that they are an intrusive, unwanted behavior that you are trying to resist, or do they feel like a natural, even appropriate, way for you to interact with your environment?

I don't really try to fight or resist the urge; it just feels like something I have to do in the moment before I can move on. Even though I know it looks strange to customers and holds up the line, it feels completely necessary to do before I can bag the items.

Do you feel that your need to tap and line up items is a personal quirk or a way of expressing your unique personality, or do you feel that these actions are becoming a strange, disorganized disruption to your daily life?

No, it definitely doesn't feel like a personal quirk or a way of expressing myself; it just feels like a strange, disruptive urge. It has become a real problem at work because it holds up the line, and it has actually led to me getting write-ups from my manager.

When you exhibit these repetitive movements and freezing, do you experience a loss of emotional expression, such as a lack of facial movement or a monotone voice, that persists even when you are not performing these rituals?

Yes, even when I'm not freezing or tapping, I feel a general flatness and lack the energy to express myself. I've stopped caring about things I used to love, like playing my bass, and I barely speak unless someone asks me a direct question because it takes too much effort to get the words out. This lack of interest and difficulty connecting with others has been going on for over two years now.

When you experience these periods of freezing or repetitive movements, do you remain completely unresponsive to people talking to you, or can you still hear and understand what is happening around you?

I'm not entirely sure how responsive I am during those freezing moments, because I completely lose track of time. It feels like only a few seconds to me, but then I "snap back" and see customers waving or asking if I'm okay, so I realize it was much longer. I'm really not sure if I can actually hear them while it's happening or if I just completely zone out.

During these episodes where you freeze or perform rituals, do you find yourself adopting and holding unusual or rigid body postures for extended periods, or do you simply find it difficult to initiate movement?

It's not really about holding rigid postures or having trouble starting to move. It's more that I suddenly freeze or pause right in the middle of an action, like holding a can in midair or staring at the barcode scanner. To me, it only feels like a few seconds, even though it's long enough for customers to notice and ask if I'm okay.
Do you ever find that you automatically repeat or echo words spoken to you by others, or do you find yourself mimicking the movements or gestures of the people around you?
No, I don't think I do that. I haven't noticed myself repeating what other people say or copying their movements.

When you are in these states of freezing or performing your rituals, do you find yourself following instructions from others, or do you feel a sense of resistance or 'negativism' where you feel compelled to do the opposite of what is asked of you?

I don't really feel like I'm trying to resist anyone or follow specific instructions during those moments. I just feel completely zoned out or 'stuck' in my own head, and I'm not really sure how else to describe it.

Do you ever find that you maintain a rigid, fixed body position for a long time, or do you have periods where you show a significant lack of response to your environment, such as not reacting to physical touch or loud sounds?

I do experience moments where I catch myself standing perfectly still, frozen mid-action like holding a can in midair or staring at the barcode scanner. It only feels like a few seconds to me, but it lasts long enough that customers have to wave or ask if I'm okay to get me to snap out of it. I don't think I hold rigid positions for a really long time beyond those freezing moments.
